strategies.name: Momentum
strategies.best_for: The first hour of the session, when news and volume drive fast moves.
strategies.risk: Chasing a move that has already run out of steam.
rules: Wait for a candle to close above the highest high (or below the lowest low) of the previous 4 candles.
RSI must show strength: 60 or more to buy, 40 or less to sell.
Price must be on the same side of VWAP, and volume at least 1.5x its usual for that time of day.
Stop 0.75% from entry (0.3% on indices), target 1.5x the risk.
Leave early if RSI falls back through 50, which means the momentum has faded.
strategies.verdict: After estimated costs Momentum lost ₹486,063 over 4382 trades (33.1% winners). It was behind even before costs. Neither half of the period was profitable. There is no sign of an edge here yet.

strategies.name: Breakout
strategies.best_for: A stock that has gone quiet in a tight range and then breaks out on heavy volume.
strategies.risk: False breakouts that snap straight back into the range.
rules: Find a tight range: the last six 15-minute candles together span no more than 0.9% (0.45% on indices).
A 15-minute candle must close outside the range with at least 2x the volume of the range candles.
Stop at the middle of the range, target 1.5x the range height beyond the breakout.
Skip if the move has already gone a full range height past the level.
strategies.verdict: After estimated costs Breakout lost ₹380,315 over 3657 trades (38.7% winners). Before costs it was ahead by ₹88,371, so trading costs took all of it. Neither half of the period was profitable. There is no sign of an edge here yet.

strategies.name: Reversal
strategies.best_for: A sharp over-extended move that shows signs of running out of fuel.
strategies.risk: Stepping in front of a move that keeps going. The article rates this the second hardest strategy.
rules: The stock must be at least 2% (0.8% for indices) away from today's open, in one direction.
RSI must have reached an extreme (25 or less, or 75 or more) in the last 3 candles.
The latest candle must show rejection: a hammer or shooting star wick, or an engulfing candle.
Trade against the move. Target is VWAP, stop is just past the extreme; skip unless the reward is at least 1.2x the risk.
strategies.verdict: After estimated costs Reversal lost ₹192,035 over 1727 trades (25.6% winners). It was behind even before costs. Neither half of the period was profitable. There is no sign of an edge here yet.

strategies.name: VWAP pullback
strategies.best_for: A steady trending day where price keeps returning to the day's average price line.
strategies.risk: Choppy days when price keeps crossing VWAP back and forth.
rules: Price must have stayed on one side of VWAP for at least 5 of the previous 6 candles.
It must have moved at least 0.3% (0.15% on indices) away from VWAP in the last hour.
Then a candle pulls back to touch VWAP and closes back on the trend side, in the trend's direction.
Stop just beyond the pullback extreme, target 2x the risk.
strategies.verdict: After estimated costs VWAP pullback lost ₹1,189,681 over 14602 trades (34.6% winners). Before costs it was ahead by ₹117,974, so trading costs took all of it. Neither half of the period was profitable. There is no sign of an edge here yet.

strategies.name: Gap and go
strategies.best_for: Stocks that open far from yesterday's close on news and keep going.
strategies.risk: The gap fills and price drifts back to yesterday's close.
rules: The stock must open at least 1% (0.5% for indices) away from yesterday's close.
Volume in the first 15 minutes must be at least 2x normal.
The gap must hold: less than half of it may be filled in the first 15 minutes.
After the 15-minute wait, enter when a candle closes beyond the first 15-minute high (gap up) or low (gap down).
Stop at the middle of the first 15-minute range, target 2x the risk.

strategies.name: Opening range breakout
strategies.best_for: Liquid large stocks and indices on days that trend from the open.
strategies.risk: Range-bound days where price pokes out of the range and falls back.
rules: Mark the high and low of the first 15 minutes (9:15 to 9:30).
Skip the day if that range is wider than 2.5% (0.6% on indices).
Enter when a 5-minute candle closes outside the range, once per direction per day.
Stop at the opposite end of the range, target 1.5x the range height beyond the breakout.
strategies.verdict: After estimated costs Opening range breakout lost ₹708,437 over 9993 trades (46.3% winners). Before costs it was ahead by ₹143,680, so trading costs took all of it. Neither half of the period was profitable. There is no sign of an edge here yet.

strategies.name: Bollinger bounce
strategies.best_for: Ranging, sideways markets. The strategy switches itself off when the market is trending (ADX 22 or more).
strategies.risk: Band walking: in a strong trend price rides the band and the bounce never comes.
rules: Only trade when ADX is below 22, meaning the market is not trending.
The previous candle must have closed outside a Bollinger band (20 candles, 2 standard deviations) and this candle closes back inside it, in the bounce direction.
Skip if price was already outside the band for the two candles before that (band walking).
Target the middle band; stop half a typical candle range past the extreme. Skip unless reward is at least 1x risk.
strategies.verdict: After estimated costs Bollinger bounce lost ₹314,098 over 3535 trades (36.1% winners). Before costs it was ahead by ₹15,521, so trading costs took all of it. Neither half of the period was profitable. There is no sign of an edge here yet.

strategies.name: Bollinger squeeze breakout
strategies.best_for: Low-volatility consolidation just before a big expansion.
strategies.risk: Fake breakouts: the squeeze breaks one way, traps traders, and reverses.
rules: The Bollinger bands must have been squeezed (at their narrowest in the last 100 candles) for at least 3 of the last 6 candles.
Then the first candle to close outside a band, with volume at least 1.3x normal for that time.
Stop at the middle band, target 2x the risk.
strategies.verdict: After estimated costs Bollinger squeeze breakout lost ₹202,446 over 2252 trades (34.0% winners). Before costs it was ahead by ₹46,474, so trading costs took all of it. Neither half of the period was profitable. There is no sign of an edge here yet.

strategies.name: EMA 9/21 crossover
strategies.best_for: The early phase of a new trend. It switches itself off in sideways markets using ADX.
strategies.risk: Whipsaws: frequent false crosses in choppy conditions.
rules: The 9-period exponential average must cross the 21-period average, with price on the same side of the 21.

strategies.name: EMA trend pullback
strategies.best_for: Established strong trends, bullish or bearish. The strategy only works when ADX is 22 or more.
strategies.risk: Missing the trade if the trend is too strong to ever pull back.
rules: The 20-period average must be above the 50-period (below it for sells), and the 50-period must be sloping the same way.
ADX must be at least 22, and price on the trend side of the 50-period average.
A candle dips to the 20-period average and closes back above it (below it for sells), in the trend's direction.
Stop half a typical candle range past the dip extreme, target 2x the risk. Exit early if price closes through the 50-period.
strategies.verdict: After estimated costs EMA trend pullback lost ₹1,130,187 over 12848 trades (31.4% winners). Before costs it was ahead by ₹71,214, so trading costs took all of it. Neither half of the period was profitable. There is no sign of an edge here yet.

assumptions: Each trade risks about ₹500 on a share (position capped at ₹40,000) or one lot of an index future, so results are comparable between strategies.
Shares are bought or sold intraday. Index trades use the index level as a stand-in for the futures price.
Costs deducted: ₹40 plus 0.03% of turnover and 0.03% slippage per leg on shares; ₹80 plus 0.02% and 0.01% slippage per leg on index futures.
A signal is acted on at the close of the candle that produced it. When one candle touches both the stop and the target, the stop is assumed to have been hit first.
Indicators use only past candles. Index volume does not exist, so volume checks are skipped for indices and their average price line is a plain average.
No setting was tuned to this data. Every number is the one set out on the strategy's tab.
All open trades are closed by 15:15.
